findings.claim: The new acceptance regex `(^|[^\w-])gentle-ai([^\w-]|$)` matches the word `gentle-ai` in any position of a hook command, including as a path segment or argument (for example `~/.gentle-ai/x` or `--home /opt/gentle-ai/`). A labdrian-owned `gentle-ai-overlay` hook command that carries such a path would be reported as invoking the binary, which makes the acceptance check fail with a false positive. The earlier wording (first token's basename) did not have this problem. The text names only the `-overlay` suffix as the exclusion, and the regex was tested on seven samples that contain no such path.

evidence: The diff changes S17 acceptance (line 34) and appends L24; the L24 claim of five matches and two non-matches is consistent with the regex as written (5+2=7).

Regex semantics: `/` and `.` and `|` are not word characters or `-`, so they count as boundaries. This is why the regex matches the timeout, pipe and `&&` samples, and also why it would match path segments.
